subject: NovaCheckout: deployment-mode recommendation after discovery
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@novacheckout.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-29T15:02:00Z
Subject: NovaCheckout: deployment-mode recommendation after discovery

Hi Tom — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary from our call:
- Latency target: p95 inference <= 60ms for the storefront scoring path (hard SLO).
- Expected steady-state QPS: 400–600; peak bursts up to ~1,100 for flash sales (peaks ~10–15 minutes).
- Typical request: 12–18 tokens output, ~70 tokens input (average).
- Model: you indicated you want to use the open Llama-3-13B-v2 variant for now.
- Security: data residency within US and audit logs required; no full air-gapped constraint.

Primary question we left on the table: whether to start on Redwood Hosted API (fastest onboarding) vs Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) vs Private VPC (not required initially).

What we recommend next (asks):
1) Can you share a short QPS/time profile CSV we can use to simulate burst shape? (attached: example template).
2) Confirm model name and whether quantized weights are acceptable for first pilot.
3) Are you open to a 3-week Dedicated pilot (we can reserve a pool sized for your 1,100 peak) vs starting on Hosted with a staged ramp?

Attachments: redwood-pilot-proposal.pdf (proposal + pilot options), example_qps_template.csv

I can loop Ben from Solutions to outline conservative config and cost delta. Proposed timeline: pilot kickoff within 2 business weeks after we get QPS profile and model confirmation.

Thanks,
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Jasmine — thanks for the clear summary. Attach: nova_qps_profile.csv (real 7‑day sample). A few clarifications inline: 

- The 1,100 peak is accurate but only during promo windows (roughly 2–3 times per quarter). The more common peak is ~750 sustained for up to 45 minutes.
- We can confirm Llama-3-13B-v2 as the model; quantized (int8) is fine for the pilot if throughput/cost looks reasonable.
- Audit logs and US residency required; VPC only if we see latency variance in pilot.

Please review the attached QPS file and recommend pilot sizing. We prefer to avoid a long procurement cycle — a short Dedicated pilot with an option to convert to Reserved would be ideal.

—Tom

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom@novacheckout.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T11:12:00Z
Subject: Re: NovaCheckout: deployment-mode recommendation after discovery — pilot sizing & recommendation

Hi Tom / Jasmine / Marissa — reviewed the QPS sample. Short summary and recommendation: 

Assessment (high level):
- Steady-state 400–600 QPS with ~45min spikes to 700–800 and rare promos hitting 1,100.
- Model: Llama-3-13B-v2 quantized (int8) is achievable with current runtime optimizations; expected per-token latency difference vs fp16 is small for server-side batching.

Recommendation: Start with a Dedicated pilot sized for your typical bursts (target configuration below) and enable a Hosted fallback route for headroom during promotional peaks. Rationale:
- Dedicated gives predictable p95 tail latency and consistent token economics for sustained traffic.
- Hosted fallback enables you to absorb unplanned traffic spikes without long procurement.

Pilot configuration (conservative):
- Fleet: 4x H100 80GB (dedicated pool).
- Expected concurrency per GPU: 6–8 concurrent requests tuned via continuous batching (target avoid big batching at tail).
- Expected p95: 40–55ms for the scoring path at typical request sizes (based on 13B int8 with our batching profile).
- Autoscale policy: add 2 GPUs at 10‑minute sustained CPU/GPU utilization > 70% or queue depth threshold.

Cost/Timeline:
- Pilot: 3 weeks active + 1 week validation (4 weeks total).
- Rough pilot cost delta vs Hosted: Dedicated pilot ~1.6x hosted per-token cost for the reserved period but yields better tail stability. Exact pricing in attached estimate.

Required from NovaCheckout to finalize sizing:
1) Confirm average tokens per request & any long-context samples.
2) Confirm acceptable model variant (you said Llama-3-13B-v2 int8).
3) Provide a small set (10–20) of production prompts to sanity-check prompt engineering for latency.

Attachments: dedicated-config-estimate.xlsx (cost and capacity sheet).

Next steps:
- If you agree, I’ll prepare the pilot contract (covers Dedicated pool + Hosted fallback) and schedule a kickoff the week of July 12.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
